precepts.why:
“But if a man find a betrothed damsel in the field, and the man force her, and lie with her: then the man only that lay with her shall die: But unto the damsel thou shalt do nothing; there is in the damsel no sin worthy of death: for as when a man riseth against his neighbour, and slayeth him, even so is this matter:”

Tamar told Amnon, “Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.” She herself calls it folly, a sin, a thing that ought not to be done in Israel. “Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice: but, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.”

The law settles it: the man who forces a damsel is worthy of death, and there is no sin in her. Any man talking about forcing a woman is wicked. This shows plainly from the scriptures that rape is not good in the Bible. It is the same as murder.

points: Amnon fell sick with lust for his sister Tamar, and Jonadab, a subtle friend, gave him the devil's counsel to feign sickness and get her alone; the counsellor who is supposed to give godly counsel can tell you how to be the devil.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

points: Tamar said no such thing ought to be done in Israel and thou shalt be as one of the fools in Israel; he would not hearken because the lust demon was on him, and forced her.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

points: Then he hated her more than he had loved her: post-clarity, when the demon leaves and reality hits. The same happens after a hasty decision or after sex: you cannot test drive a wife, and the regret becomes arguments that never stop.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

points: Before the 1800s brides wore their best dress in blue, red, gold, black, or pattern; white stained and was expensive. The white dress comes from Queen Victoria's 1840 wedding to Prince Albert, a royal fashion trend copied across Europe and America that signalled money and standing, not purity.

Tamar had a garment of divers colours upon her, for with such robes were the king's daughters that were virgins apparelled. Many colours symbolized purity, not white. Psalms 45:13-14: the king's daughter is all glorious within, her clothing of wrought gold, brought unto the king in raiment of needlework. Ornate, patterned, and biblical.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Absalom the son of David had a fair sister named Tamar, and Amnon the son of David loved her, and was so vexed for her that he fell sick, for she was a virgin and he thought it hard to do anything to her. Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother, who was a very subtle man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Jonadab asked Amnon why he, the king's son, was lean from day to day, and Amnon confessed he loved Tamar. Jonadab told him to lie down and make himself sick, and when David came to see him, to ask that Tamar come and dress meat in his sight that he might eat at her hand.

This was the fastest, sneakiest advice: play sick, and when your father comes to check on you, say you just want to eat cakes from Tamar's hand. David sent home to Tamar and told her to go dress her brother meat.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Tamar went to Amnon's house, took flour, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight and baked them, but he refused to eat and commanded every man out from him. Then he told Tamar to bring the meat into the chamber that he might eat of her hand, and when she brought it, he took hold of her and said, Come lie with me, my sister.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Tamar answered, Nay, my brother, do not force me, for no such thing ought to be done in Israel, do not thou this folly. But he would not hearken to her voice, and being stronger than she, forced her and lay with her.

Tamar herself calls this folly, a sin, a thing that ought not to be done in Israel. Any man talking about forcing a woman is wicked; this shows plainly from the scriptures that rape is not good in the Bible. It is the same as murder.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: After he forced her, Amnon hated her exceedingly, so that the hatred was greater than the love he had for her, and he told her to arise and be gone. Tamar said the evil of sending her away was greater than the other he had done, but he would not hearken, and called his servant to put her out and bolt the door after her. She had a garment of diverse colours, for so were the king's daughters that were virgins apparelled.

The king's daughters that were virgins, meaning those able to be married, dressed a certain way, in a garment of diverse colours, so you could tell them apart from the other women. That was part of the order in the kingdom, and it is why we wear garments today; the men back in the day did the same thing, and that is called rehearsing the righteous acts.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Tamar put ashes on her head, rent her garment of diverse colours, laid her hand on her head, and went out crying. Absalom her brother asked whether Amnon her brother had been with her, told her to hold her peace for now since he was her brother, and Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom's house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom, her older brother, told her not to worry about it for now. But Absalom was one of those men who holds a grudge for years just to get someone back for it, and remember these are people who know the law and know they are Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: When King David heard all these things he was very wroth. And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had forced his sister Tamar.
David was upset at what happened to Tamar but did not do anything about it. Absalom said nothing to Amnon, but he was quietly holding on to the offense, waiting.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: After two full years Absalom had sheepshearers in Baalhazor beside Ephraim and invited all the king's sons. He pressed David to come, and when David would not, he pressed that Amnon and all the king's sons go with him, and the king let them go.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom was setting Amnon up. He specifically maneuvered to get Amnon out of the city and among his own servants.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom told them to wait until Amnon was drunk and merry with wine, then to strike, and killed him for what he did to Tamar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom commanded his servants to mark when Amnon's heart was merry with wine, and when he gave the word to smite and kill him, to fear not, for he had commanded them. The servants did as Absalom commanded, and all the king's sons arose, every man got upon his mule, and fled.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: While they were on the way, tidings came to David that Absalom had slain all the king's sons and not one was left. The king arose, tare his garments, and lay on the earth. But Jonadab said not to suppose all were slain, for Amnon only was dead; by the appointment of Absalom this had been determined from the day Amnon forced his sister Tamar.
The report was exaggerated, so David thought all his sons were dead. Jonadab corrected him: only Amnon was dead, and it was because of what Amnon had done to Tamar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Understand the mind of David: even through what he was going through, and even though many of his sons did wicked things, he still showed compassion. This is why the Most High said David is a man after his own heart; even through all our rebellion, the Most High still shows us mercy.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom fled, and the watchman saw much people coming, and Jonadab confirmed the king's sons had come as he said. The king's sons came, lifted up their voice and wept, and the king and all his servants wept very sore. Absalom fled to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, and David mourned for his son every day, and was there three years; and the soul of David longed to go forth to Absalom, being comforted concerning Amnon since he was dead.
